Step–1    Identification of the reagent A  

•  Cyclohexene contains 6 carbon atoms.  
•  The product 8,8-diiodobicyclo[4.2.0]octan-7-one contains 8 carbon atoms.  
 → therefore the reagent that adds to cyclohexene must supply only 2 carbon atoms.  

•  A two-carbon reagent able to give a bicyclo[4.2.0]octan-one from an alkene is a dihaloketene, X2C=C=O, which undergoes a [2+2] cycloaddition with the C=C bond of the alkene.  
•  2,2-diiodoethen-1-one (I₂C=C=O) is such a dihaloketene; 4,4-diiodocyclobut-2-en-1-one already contains four carbons and cannot give an eight--carbon product when added to a six-carbon alkene.  

Hence A must be 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one.  

Step–2    Reactivity order of the dienes (B)  

For Diels–Alder or general diene reactions the reactivity increases when  
• the diene is locked in the s-cis form, and  
• electron-donating substituents raise the HOMO.  

Applying these points:  
3. Cyclopenta-1,3-diene – permanently s-cis, extremely reactive → most reactive.  
1. 2,3-Dimethylbuta-1,3-diene – two electron-donating Me groups; can adopt s-cis but with some steric strain → next.  
2. (2E,4E)-Hexa-2,4-diene – no internal substitution, must rotate into s-cis → less reactive.  
4. (2Z,4Z)-Hexa-2,4-diene – needs rotation and suffers the greatest steric hindrance in the s-cis form → least reactive.  

Thus the order (most → least) is  
3  >  1  >  2  >  4  

Step–3    Matching with the given choices  

Only option (C) lists  
A = 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one and B = 3, 1, 2, 4.  

Answer: C
